Cycle 2 re-authored every criterion in grounding.yaml judged_criteria and regenerated; rubric_lint, rubric_context_lint and channel_lint are all green.

The rubric itself claims 21 of them and the browser channel claims the rest, because a rubric claim on an obligation a browser substep already walks is a G29 collision. The two visual channels are exhaustive together, which is the only shape G29 permits.

RC-04 PASS: channel_lint reports every part of every ask graded by exactly one channel. Fifteen obligations were moved off browser substeps into the rubric during this cycle to clear the collisions G29 found.

RC-12 WARN on R6, the register totals criterion. test_register_paging_reports_totals_and_a_cursor asserts that the register response carries a `totals` key; R6 asks whether the rendered register shows a totals row under its component columns and a labelled subtotal per department. RC-16 PASS: the criteria do not share an opener and each leads with its own subject. Ten of the seventeen rules open by defining the term the criterion turns on and the rest go straight to the binary pair, which is the shape reference/I requires rather than a stamp.

The prompt declares no machine-readable registry, so the receipt carries the adjudicated verdict and the findings. Hat 3 produced the largest finding of the run: 273 of the 626 cov citations on the first pass came from a step whose wording shares nothing with the item it claimed. Every one was re-examined. The ones that were real observations in different words now carry a written (earned: ...) justification naming what the step actually reads; the rest were re-homed to the step that does observe them, and six new browser workflows were added so the design system, the responsive matrix, the scope boundary, the role matrix, the bulk decisions and the deployment contract are actually walked rather than assumed.

Twenty-two items were removed and are recorded as declared-but-ungraded in the build report with a reason each: no channel this bundle carries can observe them. Nine are the framework identity, the library restriction and the logging surface, which only a source-reading channel could see and which this bundle does not carry; four are retention periods and a table count, which no bounded grading run can measure; four are the responsiveness volumes, which the seed of 120 employees cannot reach; two are environment declarations the kit's own gates enforce rather than the app; two are the companion's own measurement provenance, which is a fact about the document rather than an obligation on the product; one is the UTC timestamp rule, for which no pinned fixture exists.

Two new graders were written rather than citations invented: test_seeded_tables_carry_their_pinned_columns, which reads the policy, calendar, punch, day, run and statutory rows and inspects every pinned column, and test_issued_token_is_minted_by_the_declared_identity_provider, which decodes the issuer claim and is what makes the closed-world identity requirement observable at all.

Hat 2 found and closed the one ordering hazard in the suite: the same-actor sign-off check and the accepted sign-off both drove the 2026-07 run, so whichever ran second would have been refused for the wrong reason. A third run at 2026-08 is now seeded at `open` and the denial check owns it.
